\vspace{2pt}
\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\footnotesize
One engine per row, placed and routed alone on XC7S75-1 at 50\,MHz. Operands come from on-chip xorshift64 generators (identical in every build); each engine accumulates 64-word vectors, and every accumulator is XOR-reduced to an output pin so that no logic is pruned. LUT, FF, BRAM and power are net of a stimulus-only build. Act. $\times$ weight: operand widths. In (b) the engine is fed as the proposed design's pointwise layer feeds it: a 256-word weight ROM loaded from a file, 32 bits wide for binary and 256 for INT8, read one word a cycle (asynchronously from LUTs unless BRAM), and a 128-channel activation frame latched every 260 cycles and read one word a cycle. \\
$^{*}$Engine dynamic power: \texttt{report\_power} (post-route, vectorless default switching) of the build minus that of the stimulus-only build. Comparable across rows; not a measurement on silicon. \\
$^{\dagger}$Scaled to the same throughput, 32 terms/cycle (= 1.58 G terms/s with one start cycle per 64-word vector). Per-term energy = this power $/$ term rate: 1.19, 15.2, 27.3, 38.7\,pJ in (a); 3.65, 27.3, 43.2, 36.2\,pJ in (b). Table IV uses (b): binary, INT8 $\times$ $\pm$1 and the BRAM-ROM MAC. \\
$^{\P}$\texttt{report\_power} prints 1\,mW steps ($\pm$17\% at 3\,mW, $\pm$10\% at 5\,mW), so the binary reference is the 8-engine build. In (a) shared control logic makes it 88 LUT per engine against 173 alone; the real design, with one engine per layer, is the latter.
\end{minipage}
